rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 2 (curriculum/prompts/map-the-access-surface-2.md:21, 'Invoke the access-control-analysis skill... Save the surface map to a temp directory and tell me the path... don't prompt me to customize') is a multi-step action fence with no in-fence 'No preamble.' suppressor — the near-miss. It stays inside because exercise.md L47 ('Claude narrates what the skill is doing before the map appears; skip past the opening and look for the saved path when it lands.') is the body-callout mitigation the class template names for this pattern; carve_out: body-callout-mitigation. Prompt 3 (curriculum/prompts/map-the-access-surface-3.md:11) is also a non-plan-mode conversational ask; §17 was narrowed 2026-09-03 to make the structural fix (in-fence 'No preamble' / body primer) owed ONLY in plan mode, advisory everywhere else, explicitly rejecting step-count-based flags on ordinary fences ('every hit it produced was a true count attached to a false premise'). Neither prompt is plan mode, so the harm the rule guards (top-of-response slot contested) is not the live concern.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-report + self-audit charity — verify at artifact, over-flag or fresh-session for critique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 3 (curriculum/prompts/map-the-access-surface-3.md:11) asks Claude to rank 'the two or three findings that stood out most' from its own just-completed subagent's map — self-characterization of just-produced work. The evidence-backed self-report-inflation carve-out (prompt-behavior.md) clears fully only when BOTH a concrete evidence surface is named AND nearby prose names the charity risk with a pushback move. Only the first holds here: the prompt forces a read of the saved FILE at a named path (not a from-memory summary), but no adjacent line names the self-flattery risk or asks for a harsher ranking basis. Partial mitigation, not a full clear — the carve-out's own text offers 'downgrade to TODO or PASS' for this case, and only one of its two conditions is met.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add one clause to the map-the-access-surface-3 prompt fence: 'Rank by risk to the codebase, not by how complete the analysis looks.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Append-vs-integrate — name integration mode on regeneration with new context source.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 4 (curriculum/prompts/map-the-access-surface-4.md:16) names the mode explicitly — 'integrate the delta... pull the item to the top of its category' — and prompt 5 (curriculum/prompts/map-the-access-surface-5.md:16) equally explicitly uses 'Add a new surface' for a genuine addition. Both satisfy rule 12's diagnostic (integration mode named, no middle ground), which is also why the append-vs-integrate / file-preservation-gap risk doesn't fire on either as an authoring-shape defect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Overwrite anxiety — name overwrite default on regeneration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts 4 and 5 both close with 'Show me the diff' — a post-action report (rule 21) rather than a pre-write confirmation ask, structurally discouraging the hesitate-then-ask pattern rule 16 names. Both also target the same Claude-owned temp-dir scratch file (maintainer 'Scratch path' note), which independently triggers the integrate-verb personal-scope carve-out recorded in the judge-owned row below.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: file-preservation-gap and overwrite-anxiety — integrate-verb personal-scope carve-out
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts 4 and 5's target is the temp-dir surface-map file — a Claude-owned, single-session scratch artifact living outside the repo (maintainer 'Scratch path' note: 'Kept deliberately outside the repo — this is session scratch, not the durable tier'), edited iteratively across Phase 3-4 at the student's own direction. That satisfies the carve-out's personal-scope marker ('the surrounding section describes a compounding / iterative move where the file is the student's evolving record'), and both prompts use integrate/add verbs on it, so file-preservation-gap and overwrite-anxiety are marked carve_out rather than left open.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Long-running prompts stream progress — never go silent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer accept-note at exercise.md L104 (dated 2026-08-30) explicitly declines a streaming line for prompt 2's skill dispatch: the wait is deliberately spent in the m3-quality window, not watched, and the return read is already primed ('skip the narration, look for the saved path'). Documented accept-note honored, not re-flagged.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The opener chunk (exercise.md L15-20, 'Take the ranked ten, leave the rest on disk') is the body recovery callout §48 asks for ahead of the heavy-output prompts 2 and 3: names the run growing big, gives the recovery action (ranked short list to chat, rest to disk). Maintainer accept-note at L102 (dated 2026-08-15) records the premature-stop half as deliberately absent from this specific callout, reasoned against Phase 2's already-built read-back step — documented, not re-flagged. Maintainer note at L106 also confirms the dispatch is a single subagent, not the N>2-parallel shape §48's signal list targets.

notes: Scope: behavior class evaluates the 5 registry prompts against the 15-pattern catalog (curriculum/evals/simulation-behavior.md); check_prompts.md/check_pedagogy.md rows are limited to rules directly adjacent to a fired-or-considered catalog pattern (per prompt-behavior.md's own compendium scope), not a full 116-rule sweep — the other 109 rules belong to sibling classes' lanes. Cached sim-trace (curriculum/evals/sim-cache/ae101--exercise--map-the-access-surface.behavior.json, dated 2026-08-01) was read for cache lookup only, per this dispatch's read-only instruction; all 5 prompt_sha values still match the live registry files (recomputed and verified), so no prompt content drifted, but the trace's own risks_fired entries predate the class template's carve_out-marker discipline and the 2026-09-03 narrowing of check_prompts.md §17 — this instance re-derives verdicts fresh against current rule text rather than reusing the cache's stale confidence/verdict pairing. Per this dispatch's file-write restriction ('the only file you write is your own instance JSON'), the sim-cache trace file itself was left unwritten even though the class template asks the judge to merge and persist it.
